info.title: marimo host protocol
info.description:
The contract a marimo host serves so that other programs on the same
machine can find it, see what it has, and work with its notebooks. A
host is a program that runs marimo notebooks, such as the marimo CLI
or the VS Code extension. A client is a program that talks to a host
from the outside, such as Pair.

A host writes a small file, the host record, that says where its API
is and how to authenticate. A client reads that file, opens the host's
event stream to learn what it has, and calls the operations the host
lists. There are two streams: `/events` carries the catalog, and
`/notebooks/{notebook_id}/events` carries one notebook: its cells and
document, its runtime, and the runs of code against it. Clients ignore
fields, operation names, event
names, and problem types they do not recognize. A host rejects a request
body that has a member it does not recognize. A change that would
break an existing client requires a new record version and a new base
path.

schema.description:
A key the client makes up for this request, such as a UUID. It
does two jobs. If the client sends the same request again, for
example after a timeout, the host returns the original response
instead of doing the work twice. And the host puts the key on
every event about the object the request changed, as
`request_id`, until that object reaches a final status, so the
client can tell which changes it caused. Sending the same key with
a different request is a `conflict`. Keys are scoped to the host,
across all mutation routes, for a host-documented retry window
independent of result and replay retention. Repeating a run request
returns its latest run record, even if its outputs have expired.
Outside that window or after loss of host state, the key may execute
again. Error responses do not reserve a key. Clients use fresh keys
for new work and decision retries.

201.description:
A notebook is a document and its results as the host knows them,
usually backed by a file. Its kernel, when it has one, is a
separate object, the runtime.

post.description:
Adds an empty notebook to the project. The request carries the
notebook's own fields, and the host fills in what it owns. In a
project with a `root`, `path` is required and `name` defaults to
the filename; if a file already exists at `path`, the host
answers `conflict` and leaves it alone. In a project without a
root, `name` is required, the host chooses storage, and `path` is
null. A request missing the required field is `invalid-request`.
The new notebook appears on the catalog stream with this
request's key.

Which kinds to send, as a comma-separated list of kind names such as `runtime,project`. Omit it to receive every kind the stream carries.

get.description:
Sends everything the host has, then every change as it happens.
The response is a stream of server-sent events, so it stays open
and the host appends one event at a time. The catalog is the host
object, its projects, notebooks, runtimes, and attachments.

A new connection starts with one event per object the host knows
about, parents before children, followed by a `ready` event.
Snapshot events have no `id`; `ready` and live events have an `id`
line. The most recent `id` a client has seen is its position in
the stream. When a connection drops, the client reconnects and
sends that position in the `Last-Event-ID` header. If the host
still has the events after that point, it sends them with their
original ids and timestamps, even before the new `ready`, and then
`ready`. If it does not, or the cursor predates a loss of host
state, it sends `reset`, and the client discards what it holds and
receives the full state again. A client also
discards an incomplete snapshot before reconnecting without a
cursor. On `reset` it clears its cursor until the next `ready`.

`kinds` limits the stream to some kinds of object without changing
ids or positions. It also filters the host object; `ready` and
`reset` are always sent. Keep the same filter when resuming a
cursor. The host writes a `: ping` comment every fifteen seconds
when nothing else is happening. A client that hears nothing for 45
seconds treats the connection as lost and reconnects.

patch.description:
Changes `path`, `name`, or both. A new `path` moves the file
under the same project root, and an attached runtime follows it.
A new `name` changes the label shown to people. What the file
contains is content, which this protocol does not write. If a
file already exists at `path`, the host answers `conflict`.

200.description: The document as an edit or save left it, or at a later revision, and the cells it touched.

400.description: The request is malformed or could not apply to any state.

401.description: The token is missing or wrong.

403.description: The request did not come from this machine, or the object's `operations` do not permit this client to call the operation.

404.description: The requested object or route was not found.

409.description: The current state does not allow the request.

412.description: The request named a state the document no longer has. The problem carries the cell and the document as they now are.

501.description: The host does not offer this operation. Its `operations` list says which it does.

post.description:
Applies an ordered list of changes to the document as one unit.
Preconditions are checked against the document as it was when the
request arrived. `create_cell` requires a new id and appends the
cell. To place it elsewhere, include a later `set_order` with the
order etag the client read. `replace_cell` replaces an existing
cell in place. Cells and the order have separate etags. Use `*` to skip
the etag check.

If any precondition is stale, nothing is applied and the host
answers `precondition-failed`. Its `index` names the first stale
change, and it carries the cell and the document as they now
are. A change that could not apply to any state, such as an
order that leaves out a cell or names one twice, is
`invalid-request`.

On success the document has changed, and every attachment sees
the effects on the notebook's stream with this request's key: the
cells that changed, `cell.removed` for each deleted cell, and then
the document, with nothing in between. The response carries the new
etags, as of this edit or a later revision, so a client keeps editing without reading again. A
change that changes nothing keeps its etags and sends no events.
Whether the result has reached the store shows in the document's
`saved_etag`.

schema.description: The notebook's id.
The `id` of the last event the client received, when reconnecting.

An opaque client identity, copied to the attachment's `identity`.
Clients can reuse it across streams and reconnects so consumers
can group their attachments within a host. It is descriptive data,
not an authentication credential or an idempotency key. Every
stream still creates its own attachment. Invalid values receive
a 400 `invalid-request` response.

What kind of client is attached, such as `browser`, `editor`, or
`agent`. Copied to the attachment's `kind`; omitted means `client`.
Hosts accept kinds they do not recognize. Values must contain one
or more lowercase ASCII letters, digits, or hyphens; invalid values
receive a 400 `invalid-request` response.

A human-readable label copied to the attachment's `name`, such as
`Notebook CLI`. Omitted or empty means the attachment's name is
null. The value must be at most 256 characters; longer values
receive a 400 `invalid-request` response.
Which kinds to send, as a comma-separated list of kind names such as `runtime,project`. Omit it to receive every kind the stream carries.
Narrows the notebook stream to one run.

get.description:
Sends the notebook, its cells and document, its runtime, its
attachments, its runs, their executions, and their items, then
every change as it happens. The
stream follows the same rules as `/events`: a snapshot that ends
in `ready`, ids as positions, `Last-Event-ID` to resume, `reset`
when the host cannot, a `: ping` comment every fifteen seconds,
and `kinds` to limit what is sent. The optional `run_id` query
narrows the stream to one run. A cursor belongs to the stream it
came from.

Opening this stream attaches the client to the notebook. An
attachment appears on both streams while the connection is open
and is removed when it closes. Every opening, including a reconnect,
creates a separate attachment. The optional
`Marimo-Attachment-Identity` header supplies its `identity` so
consumers can group connections from the same client. A shared
identity does not merge attachments or extend their lifetimes.
The snapshot includes every run that is not yet completed, with
its executions and items, plus
any completed results the host retains. Result retention is
independent of replay history. Removed objects are absent from
snapshots; a resumable stream carries their removal events.

The stream may also carry `custom` events: namespaced JSON payloads
that describe occurrences rather than object state. These have
cursors and timestamps and appear only in live delivery and replay.
A reset cannot recover custom events whose history
has expired. `kinds=custom` selects them. They do not belong to a
run and are excluded by `run_id`.

The opening phase is one consistent cut of the notebook, taken
under the lock that changes to the document take, so reading to
`ready` and closing is a snapshot, and `kinds=cell,document` is a
snapshot of the document alone. Cells arrive before the document
that orders them, in the opening phase and after every change, so
each cell named in `order` is already available to the client.
The effects of one change to the document arrive
together, with no other event between them.
get.summary: Follow one notebook as a stream

post.description:
Opens the notebook where the host normally shows notebooks, such
as a browser tab or an editor, and returns the URL it used.
Opening may start a runtime. The host omits its token from the URL,
and a client opens it exactly as given. If the notebook
cannot be shown, for example because its file is gone, the host
answers `conflict`.

200.description:
A running execution's request for a line of text. Its identity,
execution, prompt, password flag, and position stay fixed while
its status tracks the request. The record remains with its
execution after it is answered or cancelled. Submitted answers
travel through the reply endpoint to the runtime.

post.description:
Accepts an answer for delivery to the identified input and returns
identity, metadata, and updated status `answered`. Any client
permitted this operation may answer, regardless of who started
the run. The first accepted reply determines the answer.

The host returns `conflict` for a new request to an answered or
cancelled input, or `not-found` if the input is unknown, removed,
or belongs to another notebook. Retrying an accepted request with
the same key within the retry window returns the original response,
even after the execution is removed, under the protocol's
idempotency rules.

Hosts offering `runtime.run` or `runtime.execute` implement this
operation. See [Answering input](spec.md#answering-input) for delivery semantics.

202.description:
A runtime is a kernel attached to one notebook, and a notebook has
at most one. It ends when a client or the host stops it or its
process exits. The notebook keeps the ended runtime, so clients can
see how it ended, until another one starts or the notebook closes.
The host then sends `runtime.removed`. Every start and restart
creates a new runtime with a new id. Executions carry their producer's
runtime id, and their results are live while that runtime has not ended.

409.description: The current state does not allow the request. | The request needs a runtime and the notebook has none, or its runtime has ended.

post.description:
Requests interruption of active work in the notebook's current runtime,
including work with no run or execution record. Queued runs complete
cancelled without executing. The runtime stays alive. Interruption
does not roll back work already performed. Pending inputs belonging
to interrupted work are cancelled.

If the notebook has no runtime, or its runtime has ended, the host
answers `no-runtime`. If its runtime is `starting` or `stopping`, the
host answers `conflict`. An idle runtime accepts the request as a no-op
and does not arm an interrupt for future work.

The response contains the current runtime and acknowledges the request,
not that the work has stopped. Runs and executions report their actual
outcomes on the stream once they settle; acceptance alone does not
mark them cancelled. Work without a run record need not acquire one.
Within the retry window, repeating the same request returns the original
acknowledgement without interrupting again, including after new work
starts or the runtime is replaced. Hosts offering `runtime.run` or
`runtime.execute` support this operation.

202.description:
One bounded cycle of notebook work initiated by an action. It
includes synchronous callbacks and reactive work owned and awaited
by the runtime's scheduler. Context inherited by an independent task
records provenance, not ownership of the cycle. The host completes it
only after all member executions have ended and scheduling for the
cycle has finished. Completion fixes its status and execution membership.
Independently triggered later work starts another run, even when
its cause belongs to an earlier run. Every consumer attached to
the notebook sees it.

Retention is up to the host and independent of replay history.
Hosts SHOULD retain ephemeral results briefly after completion to
allow reconnection. Runs, executions, and items other than inputs each have removal
events; a cell result may outlive its run.

delete.description:
Cancels one queued or running run, leaving other runs untouched.
A queued run is removed from the queue and completes cancelled
without executing. For a running run, the host interrupts only if
that run is still active; its remaining executions end cancelled.
The host must not interrupt a successor if the target finishes before
the cancellation takes effect. A completed run receives `conflict`.
Pending inputs belonging to cancelled work are cancelled.

The response acknowledges the request, not completion. The notebook
stream carries the run and execution outcomes once they settle.
The runtime stays alive. A host that lists `runtime.run` or
`runtime.execute` supports this operation.

post.description:
Stops the runtime and starts a new one with a new id. The stream
shows the old runtime `stopping`, then `ended`, then `runtime.removed`,
then the new runtime `starting`, keeping one runtime attached to the
notebook at a time. Active and queued runs and their unfinished
executions complete with outcome `cancelled`. Retained
results stay and are no longer live. The response carries the replacement
runtime in its `starting` state. The client follows that id until
it is `ready` or has `ended`. If the notebook has no runtime, or its
runtime has ended, the host answers `no-runtime`.

post.description:
Runs the cells named in `cells` under the notebook's execution settings,
which determine whether dependent cells run too. Each execution names
its cell through `cell_id`.

Include a cell's `etag` to run it only if it still matches what the
client read. A missing or changed cell is `precondition-failed` and
nothing runs. The problem's `index` is the position of that cell
in `cells`.

Returns a `Run` with status `queued` or `running`. Cell runs and scratch
executions share one queue in acceptance order. Open the notebook
stream before submitting work to receive its progress and results.
Run and execution events carry the request's `Idempotency-Key` as
`request_id`.

A notebook without a runtime returns `no-runtime`. Within the host's
retry window, repeating the request returns its latest run record
without executing again, even if its outputs have expired.

Hosts SHOULD retain ephemeral results briefly after completion to
allow reconnection. Runs, executions, and items other than inputs each have removal
events; a cell result may outlive its run.

post.description:
Executes Python with access to the notebook's current values without
adding a cell. New variables and assignments stay within this call.
Objects are shared with the notebook, so changing a list or dataframe
can affect it.

On marimo hosts, the internal `marimo._code_mode.get_context()` API
provides access to notebook cells and captured outputs, along with
methods for editing and running cells. The outputs are captured when
execution begins.

Returns a `Run` with status `queued` or `running`. Scratch executions
and cell runs share one queue in acceptance order. Open the notebook
stream before submitting work to receive its progress and results.
The run's `origin` carries the submitted code. Run and execution events
carry the request's `Idempotency-Key` as `request_id`.

A notebook without a runtime returns `no-runtime`. Within the host's
retry window, repeating the request returns its latest run record
without executing again, even if its outputs have expired.

schema.description: The notebook's id.

A key the client makes up for this request, such as a UUID. It
does two jobs. If the client sends the same request again, for
example after a timeout, the host returns the original response
instead of doing the work twice. And the host puts the key on
every event about the object the request changed, as
`request_id`, until that object reaches a final status, so the
client can tell which changes it caused. Sending the same key with
a different request is a `conflict`. Keys are scoped to the host,
across all mutation routes, for a host-documented retry window
independent of result and replay retention. Repeating a run request
returns its latest run record, even if its outputs have expired.
Outside that window or after loss of host state, the key may execute
again. Error responses do not reserve a key. Clients use fresh keys
for new work and decision retries.

put.description:
Makes sure the notebook has a runtime that has not ended. If it has
none, or its last one ended, the host starts one and answers `202`
with the runtime `starting`. The client then follows `runtime` events
for that runtime, on either stream, until its status is `ready` or
`ended`. If the notebook already has a runtime that has not ended,
the host answers `200` with it and starts nothing.

Sometimes the host needs a choice the client did not make, such as
which environment the kernel should run in. It then answers `409`
with a problem of type `decision-required` that lists the options,
and the client repeats the request with a new `Idempotency-Key`
and `decisions` filled in. A client that already knows its choice
can include `decisions` the first time.
put.summary: Start the notebook's runtime, or find the one it has

202.description:
A runtime is a kernel attached to one notebook, and a notebook has
at most one. It ends when a client or the host stops it or its
process exits. The notebook keeps the ended runtime, so clients can
see how it ended, until another one starts or the notebook closes.
The host then sends `runtime.removed`. Every start and restart
creates a new runtime with a new id. Executions carry their producer's
runtime id, and their results are live while that runtime has not ended.

delete.description:
Ends the runtime for everyone attached to the notebook. A runtime
that is still starting is cancelled; a running kernel is shut
down. Active and queued runs and their unfinished executions complete
with outcome `cancelled`. Retained results stay
and are no longer live. The notebook and its attachments stay,
but Python state is lost. The client follows the
runtime on a stream until it has `ended`. If the notebook has no
runtime, or its runtime has ended, the host answers `no-runtime`.

post.description:
On success, `saved_etag` identifies the revision written to storage.
If the document changes during the write, its current `etag` may differ.
The client sends an empty request body because the host already holds the state. A host that persists every change as
it applies it need not offer this operation. A client shows a save control
when the notebook lists it, and reads whether anything is unsaved
from the two etags either way.

The response is an edit response, because a host may rewrite code
as it saves, for example to format it. Such changes reach the
stream like any other and the response carries the new etags.
`If-Match` makes the document etag the client last read a
precondition, and the host answers `precondition-failed` when the
document has moved on. If the store has changed since the host
last read or wrote it, the host answers `decision-required`,
offering to overwrite the store or to reload from it, and the
client repeats the request with its decision and a new key.

Event.description: A record, removal, or control message from a host stream. The data is decoded JSON. Snapshot records and reset events omit the cursor, and ready and live events carry it. Unknown event names belong to later versions or host extensions.

CatalogStreamEvent.description: Any event the catalog stream carries.

NotebookStreamEvent.description: Any event a notebook stream carries.

ObjectKind.description: The kinds a stream carries, and the values `kinds` accepts. The catalog stream carries host, project, notebook, runtime, and attachment. A notebook's stream carries notebook, document, cell, runtime, attachment, run, execution, output, console, input, variable, and custom. Custom events describe occurrences rather than object state.

version.description: The version of this record's format. This document describes version 1.

name.description: A label for the host to show people, such as `VS Code` or `marimo`. Two hosts can share a name; the filename is the identity.

url.description: Where the host's API is. The scheme is `http`, and the host part is `127.0.0.1` or `[::1]`, written exactly that way.

token.description: The secret a client sends to prove it read the record.

HostRecord.description:
A host record is the file a host writes so that clients can find
it. A host writes `<marimo-state-dir>/hosts-v1/<id>.json` once its API
is serving at `url`, where `<id>` is an identifier the host makes
up each time it starts. The record does not change while the host
runs, and the host removes it when it stops.

A client reads `version` before anything else and skips any record
it cannot parse or whose version it does not support. It also
checks that the file and its directory belong to the current user
and cannot be read by others, and that `url` points at this
machine.

Problem.description: An error. Every error response is a problem, following RFC 9457, and is served as `application/problem+json`. `type` says which. A client ignores members it does not recognize. Hosts redact tokens from errors.

type.description: What kind of problem this is, as a URI.

title.description: A short, human-readable name for the kind of problem.

status.description: The HTTP status code of the response.

detail.description: A human-readable explanation of what went wrong this time.

UnknownProblem.description: A problem of a type this version does not define. A host on a later version can send one, and a client falls back to its `status`.

index.description: The position of the first stale entry in the request, counted in an edit's `changes` or a run's `cells`. `0` for a save with a stale `If-Match`.

cell.description: The cell that entry named, as it now is. Null when the document does not have it, or when the entry named the order or the whole document.

document.description: The document as it now is.

notebook_id.description: The notebook this document belongs to.

order.description: Cell ids in display order. A permutation of the notebook's cells, each appearing exactly once.

app_config.description: Notebook-level settings, the keyword arguments to `marimo.App` such as `width` and `app_title`. Informational for now; no change sets it over this protocol.

etag.description: Identifies the document as currently applied. It changes when the order, the app config, or any cell's `etag` does.

saved_etag.description: Identifies the document as last written to the host's store, computed the same way over that state. Equal to `etag` when every accepted change has been persisted. Null when nothing has been persisted, which is the case for a scratch copy.

order_etag.description: Identifies the order alone. Editing a cell does not change it.

version.description: Counts changes to the cells, the order, or the app config. A save does not advance it. Comparable only within one notebook while it is in the catalog.

Document.description:
The document as a whole, without its cells, which are their own
objects: the cell order and app config. One per notebook,
and removed with it. The order and the app
config carry their own etags, so an edit to one does not conflict
with an edit to the other, or with edits to cells.

Etag.description: An identifier a host derives from content, so the same content has the same etag. It is opaque to clients. They read etags from the stream and from responses, and send them back as preconditions.

CellId.description: Identifies a cell within its notebook. Stable while the host serves the notebook; whether it survives a reload of the store depends on the format. `setup` is the setup cell.

NotebookId.description: Identifies a notebook. Unique within the host and unchanged while the notebook exists.

code.description: The cell's source code, with newline line endings, or null when the host does not expose source to this client. An empty string is an empty cell. A host normalizes other line endings when it loads a file. Source availability does not grant editing permission; see the notebook's operations.

name.description: The cell's name. `_` for an anonymous cell; otherwise a Python identifier, unique within the notebook.

etag.description: Precondition for edits and cell runs. Covers exact source, name, and config.

code_fingerprint.description: Fingerprint of the actual source, including when `code` is null. Formatting-only edits may preserve it. Independent of cell name, config, and source visibility.

version.description: The document version at which the cell was created or last changed.

Cell.description:
A unit of code and configuration in the document. A cell event
fires when its code, name, or config changes. Markdown and SQL
cells are code that calls `mo.md` or `mo.sql`; a client chooses
the editor to show.

CodeFingerprint.description: Opaque code identity assigned by the host. Clients compare cell and execution fingerprints for freshness. Incompatible schemes MUST produce distinct fingerprints.

column.description: The column the cell sits in, for multi-column layouts. Null in a single column.

disabled.description: Whether the cell is kept from running.

hide_code.description: Whether clients hide the code by default. This is a presentation preference; source availability is represented by `Cell.code`.

expand_output.description: Whether clients show the full output rather than a scrolled box.

CellConfig.description: How a cell is laid out and whether it runs. Every field is always present, so a cell's etag is well defined.

decisions.description: The choices the client has to make before the host can carry out the request.

id.description: Identifies the question when the client answers it.

prompt.description: The question, worded for a person.

Decision.description:
A question the host needs answered before it can carry out a
request. The client answers by repeating the request with
`decisions` in the body, mapping this `id` to the `id` of an
option.

id.description: Identifies this answer.

DecisionOption.description: One possible answer to a decision.

Process.description:
The process that wrote a record. A client checks that a process
with this `pid` that started at `started_at` still exists. If it
does not, the record is stale and may be removed.

Timestamp.description: A date and time with its offset from UTC, as RFC 3339 writes it.

id.description: The resume cursor. Omitted on snapshot and reset events.

ReadyEvent.description: The `ready` event, carried by every stream.

id.description: The resume cursor. Omitted on snapshot and reset events.

ResetEvent.description: The `reset` event, carried by every stream.

id.description: The resume cursor. Omitted on snapshot and reset events.

VariableRemovedEvent.description: The `variable.removed` event, carried by the notebook stream.

request_id.description: The `Idempotency-Key` of the request that caused this event. Omitted when no request did, and on snapshots unless that request's work is still in progress.

time.description: When the host published this event. Present on live and replayed events; omitted on snapshots.

id.description: The id of the object that was removed.

RemovedMessage.description: The data of an event ending in `.removed`. The event name identifies the kind of object to delete from the client's view. Removing a notebook also removes its document and cells, and removing an execution removes its inputs. Clients discard these child records when they receive the parent's removal event.

id.description: The resume cursor. Omitted on snapshot and reset events.

ConsoleRemovedEvent.description: The `console.removed` event, carried by the notebook stream.

id.description: The resume cursor. Omitted on snapshot and reset events.

OutputRemovedEvent.description: The `output.removed` event, carried by the notebook stream.

id.description: The resume cursor. Omitted on snapshot and reset events.

ExecutionRemovedEvent.description: The `execution.removed` event, carried by the notebook stream.

id.description: The resume cursor. Omitted on snapshot and reset events.

RunRemovedEvent.description: The `run.removed` event, carried by the notebook stream.

id.description: The resume cursor. Omitted on snapshot and reset events.

AttachmentRemovedEvent.description: The `attachment.removed` event, carried by the catalog and notebook streams.

id.description: The resume cursor. Omitted on snapshot and reset events.

RuntimeRemovedEvent.description: The `runtime.removed` event, carried by the catalog and notebook streams.

id.description: The resume cursor. Omitted on snapshot and reset events.

CellRemovedEvent.description: The `cell.removed` event, carried by the notebook stream.

id.description: The resume cursor. Omitted on snapshot and reset events.

NotebookRemovedEvent.description: The `notebook.removed` event, carried by the catalog and notebook streams.

CustomEvent.description: The `custom` event, carried by the notebook stream.

request_id.description: The `Idempotency-Key` of the request that caused this event. Omitted when no request did, and on snapshots unless that request's work is still in progress.

time.description: When the host published this event. Preserved on replay.

CustomMessage.description: The data of a `custom` event. This envelope is standardized; the custom type and payload are defined by their producer.

type.description: A namespaced event type under a namespace the producer controls, such as `marimo.pair.agent-message`. Clients ignore types they do not recognize while retaining the stream cursor.

data.description: Any JSON value, including null. The producer defines its schema and consumers of the type validate it.

Custom.description:
A notebook occurrence with a producer-defined payload. It is replayed
while event history is retained. Delivery is limited to live events
and replay on the notebook stream, with `run_id` omitted from the
stream's filters. The notebook is identified by the stream.

id.description: The resume cursor. Omitted on snapshot and reset events.

VariableEvent.description: The `variable` event, carried by the notebook stream.

request_id.description: The `Idempotency-Key` of the request that caused this event. Omitted when no request did, and on snapshots unless that request's work is still in progress.

time.description: When the host published this event. Present on live and replayed events; omitted on snapshots.

VariableMessage.description: The data of the `variable` event. The variable as it now is.

execution_id.description: The execution that bound the name.

type.description: The runtime's label for the value's type. A host may leave it null.

preview.description: A short rendering of the value. A host may leave it null.

Variable.description:
A name a cell's execution bound in the notebook's namespace, with
the revision of its value. The execution binds it as it ends, and
the item is removed with the execution. An update, as when a
state setter runs or a UI element's value changes, advances the revision
without binding again, and the producer sends the item again with
the same id. Hosts publish a cell execution's variables before its
`completed` status, and remove a cell's previous execution and
its items before publishing the next one. A scratch execution's
names live only while it runs, so it publishes no variables.

execution_id.description: The execution whose evaluation produced the value. Usually the variable's `execution_id`, and earlier when the runtime carried the value forward.

update.description: How many times the value has been updated since it was produced. Zero at binding.

Revision.description:
A variable's value at a point in time. Two revisions are equal
when `execution_id` and `update` are equal. Clients compare
revisions for equality.

ExecutionId.description: Identifies an execution. Unique within the host.

ItemId.description: Identifies an output, console, input, or variable item uniquely within the host. Sending an item again with the same id replaces it.

id.description: The resume cursor. Omitted on snapshot and reset events.

InputEvent.description: The `input` event, carried by the notebook stream.

request_id.description: The `Idempotency-Key` of the request that caused this event. Omitted when no request did, and on snapshots unless that request's work is still in progress.

time.description: When the host published this event. Present on live and replayed events; omitted on snapshots.

InputMessage.description: The data of the `input` event. The input as it now is.

id.description: Identifies this prompt uniquely across executions and runtime restarts.

seq.description: Position among the execution's console and input items, increasing in production order.

prompt.description: The prompt to display, which may be empty.

password.description: Whether clients must obscure the value as it is entered.

Input.description:
A running execution's request for a line of text. Its identity,
execution, prompt, password flag, and position stay fixed while
its status tracks the request. The record remains with its
execution after it is answered or cancelled. Submitted answers
travel through the reply endpoint to the runtime.

InputStatus.description:
An input starts `pending` while it waits for an answer. It becomes
`answered` when the host accepts a reply for delivery, or `cancelled`
when the host ends the wait while input is still pending. Both
`answered` and `cancelled` are final. An answered input stays
answered if execution later fails before consuming the value.

id.description: The resume cursor. Omitted on snapshot and reset events.

ConsoleEvent.description: The `console` event, carried by the notebook stream.

request_id.description: The `Idempotency-Key` of the request that caused this event. Omitted when no request did, and on snapshots unless that request's work is still in progress.

time.description: When the host published this event. Present on live and replayed events; omitted on snapshots.

ConsoleMessage.description: The data of the `console` event. The console as it now is.

seq.description: Position among the execution's console and input items, increasing in the order they were produced.

Console.description:
One entry in an execution's console, which is text written to
stdout or stderr, or media rendered among it. A producer replaces
an entry by sending it again with the same id, and entries are
removed with their execution.

media.description: Something rendered into the console, such as a figure from `plt.show()` or a formatted traceback.

mimetype.description: The format of `data`, such as `text/html` or `image/png`.

data.description: The rendered value, embedded so clients can display it independently of the runtime. JSON mimetypes are encoded as text and binary mimetypes as base64.

stream.description: Which stream the text went to.

id.description: The resume cursor. Omitted on snapshot and reset events.

OutputEvent.description: The `output` event, carried by the notebook stream.

request_id.description: The `Idempotency-Key` of the request that caused this event. Omitted when no request did, and on snapshots unless that request's work is still in progress.

time.description: When the host published this event. Present on live and replayed events; omitted on snapshots.

OutputMessage.description: The data of the `output` event. The output as it now is.

media.description: The output as last rendered. Null when the code set it to nothing or cleared it.

Output.description:
What an execution's code shows as its result, such as the value of
a cell's last expression. An execution has at most one, published
once the code first sets it. A producer replaces it by sending it
again with the same id, including after the execution completes,
and it is removed with its execution.

id.description: The resume cursor. Omitted on snapshot and reset events.

ExecutionEvent.description: The `execution` event, carried by the notebook stream.

request_id.description: The `Idempotency-Key` of the request that caused this event. Omitted when no request did, and on snapshots unless that request's work is still in progress.

time.description: When the host published this event. Present on live and replayed events; omitted on snapshots.

ExecutionMessage.description: The data of the `execution` event. The execution as it now is.

run_id.description: The run that owns this execution. Every live execution belongs to exactly one run. May name a run the host has dropped. Null only for a restored result whose run is unknown.

runtime_id.description: The runtime that produced this execution. Live while that runtime is the notebook's and has not ended. Null when the producer is unknown.

caused_by_id.description: The execution in the same run whose code was running when this one was scheduled, such as scratch code that ran a cell, set a UI element's value, or wrote state, and the cells that reacted to it. Null for an execution a client requested and for the cells that reacted to one.

cell_id.description: The cell this execution belongs to. Null for a scratch execution, which evaluates the code in its run's `origin`.

code_fingerprint.description: Fingerprint of the code the execution evaluates. Fixed when the execution is published, while it is still queued.

created_at.description: When the runtime scheduled this execution. Null for a restored result, whose timing is unknown.

Execution.description:
One cell evaluated within a run, or scratch code evaluated once.
It moves through `queued`, `running`, and `completed`, and ends with
one outcome. Side effects belong to the execution whose context
produced them, and items can arrive after completion while the
execution remains retained. Each new input belongs to a running
execution. Input calls from completed or removed executions raise
`EOFError` in the calling code. A scratch execution has no cell and
evaluates the code in its run's `origin`.

ExecutionState.description:
Where an execution is in its lifecycle, tagged on `status`. An
execution is `queued` until it starts, `running` while code
executes, and `completed` once it has ended with its `outcome`.

started_at.description: When the code started executing. Null if the execution never started or the start time of a restored result is unknown.

completed_at.description: When the execution ended. Null for a restored result whose store does not record it.

depends_on.description: The variable revisions this result is valid against, keyed by name. Null for a name no retained cell execution had bound. Stamped as the execution ends.

ExecutionOutcome.description:
How an execution ended, tagged on `kind`. A `succeeded` execution
evaluated its code without raising, and what it showed is its
`output` item. A `failed` execution carries the error that ended it.
A `cancelled` execution was stopped before or while it ran.
A `skipped` execution did not evaluate because of another cell; it
has no value and binds no variables. Other kinds are defined by
later versions of this protocol.

reason.description:
Why the cell did not evaluate. The string is open. This protocol
defines `upstream-failed`, a cell it depends on did not produce
its value because it raised or could not resolve a reference,
`upstream-stopped`, a cell it depends on stopped the cycle on
purpose, and `superseded`, a later execution of the same cell
replaced this one before it started because the cell's source
changed while it waited. Clients show unrecognized reasons as
skipped, with the message.

message.description: Why the cell did not run, to show in place of its output.

related.description: The cells involved, the cause first and this cell last.

range.description: Where in that cell, when known.

message.description: What that cell contributes, such as `reads x from C`.

Related.description: A cell involved in an error, possibly the one carrying it.

end.description: Exclusive end. Equal to start when only a point is known.

character.description: Zero-based offset in the line, in UTF-16 code units.

Position.description: A position within code, using LSP coordinates.

kind.description: The producer's identifier, scoped by source. Open; this protocol defines `exception` and `internal` for executions. Clients show unrecognized kinds as plain errors.

message.description: A description of the error to show people.

source.description: Who produced it, such as `marimo` or a SQL analyzer. Scopes kind.

severity.description: Error unless the producer says otherwise. Only error affects scheduling.

range.description: Where in the code, when known.

name.description: The exception class, such as `ZeroDivisionError`. Set when kind is exception, null otherwise.

traceback.description: The traceback as rendered by the runtime, plain text or HTML by its mimetype. Null when unavailable or not shown.

related.description: Every involved cell, including this one, in canonical order. Each copy of a cross-cell error carries the same list; clients deduplicate on kind and related cell ids. Empty when the error involves this code alone.

Error.description:
A problem shaped like an LSP diagnostic. Further members are
kind-specific, as in Problem Details, and a client ignores
members it does not know.

RuntimeId.description: Identifies a runtime. Unique within the host; every start and restart creates a new id.

RunId.description: Identifies a run independently of the request's `Idempotency-Key`. Events carry the key in `request_id`.

id.description: The resume cursor. Omitted on snapshot and reset events.

RunEvent.description: The `run` event, carried by the notebook stream.

request_id.description: The `Idempotency-Key` of the request that caused this event. Omitted when no request did, and on snapshots unless that request's work is still in progress.

time.description: When the host published this event. Present on live and replayed events; omitted on snapshots.

RunMessage.description: The data of the `run` event. The run as it now is.

runtime_id.description: The runtime that produced this run.

created_at.description: When the host accepted the run, or when the runtime scheduled it.

Run.description:
One bounded cycle of notebook work initiated by an action. It
includes synchronous callbacks and reactive work owned and awaited
by the runtime's scheduler. Context inherited by an independent task
records provenance, not ownership of the cycle. The host completes it
only after all member executions have ended and scheduling for the
cycle has finished. Completion fixes its status and execution membership.
Independently triggered later work starts another run, even when
its cause belongs to an earlier run. Every consumer attached to
the notebook sees it.

Retention is up to the host and independent of replay history.
Hosts SHOULD retain ephemeral results briefly after completion to
allow reconnection. Runs, executions, and items other than inputs each have removal
events; a cell result may outlive its run.

RunState.description:
Where a run is in its lifecycle, tagged on `status`. A run is
`queued` until its first execution starts and `running` until the
cycle has settled or been terminated. It is `completed` once all
member executions are terminal and no more can be scheduled in this
run, and that state is final. A run can complete with no executions.

started_at.description: When the first execution started. Null if none started.

outcome.description: An execution failure does not complete a run while other work remains. Interruption must have taken effect, not merely been requested.

RunOutcome.description:
How a run ended, tagged on `kind`. `succeeded` means its work
settled without an execution failing or being cancelled. `failed`
means an execution's code raised or the host could not finish the
cycle. An execution skipped because of another cell does not fail
its run. `cancelled` means the cycle was cut short by a cancel,
an interrupt, or its runtime stopping, even if an earlier execution
failed. Execution outcomes retain their individual results.

message.description: Why the host could not finish the cycle, to show people. Null when the run failed because an execution's code raised.

RunOrigin.description:
What a run was given when it was created, tagged on `kind`. A
`cells` run was given the cells in `cell_ids`. A `code` run was
given the code in `code`, which its scratch execution evaluates. A
`runtime` run was given neither. The runtime scheduled it in
response to a change, such as the cells that read a UI element
after its value changes. Other kinds are defined by later versions
of this protocol.

code.description: The submitted code, which the run's scratch execution evaluates.

cell_ids.description: The cells the run was requested for. Fixed when the run is accepted, so a client can tell which cells a queued run will reach before the runtime has planned their executions. Each one's execution in this run reports the fingerprint of the source accepted for it.

id.description: The resume cursor. Omitted on snapshot and reset events.

AttachmentEvent.description: The `attachment` event, carried by the catalog and notebook streams.

request_id.description: The `Idempotency-Key` of the request that caused this event. Omitted when no request did, and on snapshots unless that request's work is still in progress.

time.description: When the host published this event. Present on live and replayed events; omitted on snapshots.

AttachmentMessage.description: The data of the `attachment` event. The attachment as it now is.

identity.description:
The opaque client identity supplied by `Marimo-Attachment-Identity`.
Null when none was supplied. Consumers can group attachments
with the same identity within a host. It does not identify an
individual connection or change its lifetime.

kind.description: What kind of thing is attached, supplied by `Marimo-Attachment-Kind`, such as `browser`, `editor`, or `agent`. Defaults to `client` when the header is omitted. Clients accept kinds they do not recognize.

name.description: A label to show people, supplied by `Marimo-Attachment-Name`, such as the browser or editor's name. Null when the header is omitted or empty.

Attachment.description:
An attachment is a consumer connected to a notebook, such as a
browser tab, an editor, or an agent. Opening the notebook's stream
creates one. It is removed when that connection closes, and not
when the notebook's runtime stops or restarts. Each stream has its
own attachment, even when several share a client identity.

AttachmentId.description: Identifies an attachment. Unique within the host.

id.description: The resume cursor. Omitted on snapshot and reset events.

RuntimeEvent.description: The `runtime` event, carried by the catalog and notebook streams.

request_id.description: The `Idempotency-Key` of the request that caused this event. Omitted when no request did, and on snapshots unless that request's work is still in progress.

time.description: When the host published this event. Present on live and replayed events; omitted on snapshots.

RuntimeMessage.description: The data of the `runtime` event. The runtime as it now is.

marimo_version.description: The version of marimo running the kernel. Null until the host knows it.

created_at.description: When the host created this runtime and began starting it.

Runtime.description:
A runtime is a kernel attached to one notebook, and a notebook has
at most one. It ends when a client or the host stops it or its
process exits. The notebook keeps the ended runtime, so clients can
see how it ended, until another one starts or the notebook closes.
The host then sends `runtime.removed`. Every start and restart
creates a new runtime with a new id. Executions carry their producer's
runtime id, and their results are live while that runtime has not ended.

RuntimeState.description:
Where a runtime is in its life, tagged on `status`. A `starting`
runtime is bringing its kernel up. A `ready` runtime accepts work.
A `stopping` runtime is shutting its kernel down. An `ended`
runtime has no kernel and does not change again.

RuntimeOutcome.description:
How a runtime ended, tagged on `kind`. A `stopped` runtime was
ended by a client or the host. A `failed` runtime could not start,
or its kernel exited unexpectedly.

message.description: Why the kernel could not start or why it exited, to show people. Null when the host does not know.
A note about progress, such as the packages being installed. Null when the host has nothing to report.

id.description: The resume cursor. Omitted on snapshot and reset events.

CellEvent.description: The `cell` event, carried by the notebook stream.

request_id.description: The `Idempotency-Key` of the request that caused this event. Omitted when no request did, and on snapshots unless that request's work is still in progress.

time.description: When the host published this event. Present on live and replayed events; omitted on snapshots.

CellMessage.description: The data of the `cell` event. The cell as it now is.

id.description: The resume cursor. Omitted on snapshot and reset events.

DocumentEvent.description: The `document` event, carried by the notebook stream.

request_id.description: The `Idempotency-Key` of the request that caused this event. Omitted when no request did, and on snapshots unless that request's work is still in progress.

time.description: When the host published this event. Present on live and replayed events; omitted on snapshots.

DocumentMessage.description: The data of the `document` event. The document as it now is.

id.description: The resume cursor. Omitted on snapshot and reset events.

NotebookEvent.description: The `notebook` event, carried by the catalog and notebook streams.

request_id.description: The `Idempotency-Key` of the request that caused this event. Omitted when no request did, and on snapshots unless that request's work is still in progress.

time.description: When the host published this event. Present on live and replayed events; omitted on snapshots.

NotebookMessage.description: The data of the `notebook` event. The notebook as it now is.

path.description: The file's path relative to the project root, written the way the host's operating system writes paths. Null when the notebook has no file, such as one not yet saved, or one deleted while a runtime still refers to it.

name.description: A label to show people. Derived from the filename when the host has nothing better.

operations.description: Operations this client may call on the notebook, such as `notebook.edit` or `runtime.start`. A subset of `host.operations` selected by the client's permissions, independently of the notebook's current state. The `runtime` object shows whether a runtime is attached, and preconditions still apply when an operation is called. The host sends the notebook again when it changes.

modified_at.description: A hint of when the file was last modified, for display and ordering. It can lag, since a host need not send the notebook again when only this value changes. Null when the host does not know.

Notebook.description:
A notebook is a document and its results as the host knows them,
usually backed by a file. Its kernel, when it has one, is a
separate object, the runtime.

ProjectId.description: Identifies a project. Unique within the host and unchanged while the project exists.

id.description: The resume cursor. Omitted on snapshot and reset events.

ProjectRemovedEvent.description: The `project.removed` event, carried by the catalog stream.

id.description: The resume cursor. Omitted on snapshot and reset events.

ProjectEvent.description: The `project` event, carried by the catalog stream.

request_id.description: The `Idempotency-Key` of the request that caused this event. Omitted when no request did, and on snapshots unless that request's work is still in progress.

time.description: When the host published this event. Present on live and replayed events; omitted on snapshots.

ProjectMessage.description: The data of the `project` event. The project as it now is.

name.description: A label to show people, usually the name of the root directory.

root.description: The absolute path of the project's directory, written the way the host's operating system writes paths. Null when the project has no directory.

message.description: Why the host stopped scanning. Null unless `status` is `partial`.

operations.description: Operations this client may call on the project, today `notebook.create`. A subset of `host.operations` selected by the client's permissions, independently of the project's current state. The host sends the project again when it changes.

Project.description: A project is a group of notebooks that the host presents together, usually a directory.

ProjectStatus.description:
How far a host has gotten finding the notebooks in a project.
While it is `indexing`, more notebooks are coming. Once it is
`indexed`, the host believes it has found every notebook under the
root. A `partial` project is one the host stopped scanning on
purpose, or one with something it could not read.

id.description: The resume cursor. Omitted on snapshot and reset events.

HostEvent.description: The `host` event, carried by the catalog stream.

request_id.description: The `Idempotency-Key` of the request that caused this event. Omitted when no request did, and on snapshots unless that request's work is still in progress.

time.description: When the host published this event. Present on live and replayed events; omitted on snapshots.

HostMessage.description: The data of the `host` event. The host as it now is.

operations.description: The operations this host implements, such as `runtime.start`. Whether a client may call one on a given project or notebook is that object's `operations`. Clients accept names they do not recognize.

Host.description:
What the host can do. There is exactly one host object, and it is
the first object in a snapshot when the filter includes `host`.
A resumed stream only sends it if its operations changed since
the cursor. The host sends it again if its operations change.

path.description: The new location, relative to the project root and written the way the host's operating system writes paths.

name.description: The new label to show people.

UpdateNotebookRequest.description: The fields to change. At least one is present.

cells.description: The version of each cell the request created or changed, by id, and null for each cell it deleted.

EditResponse.description: The document as an edit or save left it, or at a later revision, and the cells it touched.

version.description: The cell's version after the edit.

CellVersion.description: A cell's etag, code fingerprint, and version after an edit.

decisions.description: Answers to the questions in a `decision-required` problem, as for `runtime.start`.

SaveRequest.description: What a save needs from the client, which is nothing until the host asks a question. `{}` is the usual body.

decisions.description:
Answers to the questions in a `decision-required` problem.
Each key is a decision's `id` and each value is the `id` of
the chosen option. A client that already knows its choices can
send them the first time.

code.description:
Python code that can read the notebook's current values.
Assignments stay local to the call. Changes to shared objects persist.

ExecuteRequest.description: Python code to execute with access to notebook values.

cells.description: Cells to run by id. The notebook's execution settings determine their order and whether dependent cells run too.

etag.description: The cell's `etag` as last read. A cell whose source, name, or config differs is `precondition-failed`. Absent, the cell runs as it is.

value.description: The text to deliver to the input exactly as submitted, including an empty string when the answer is empty.

InputReplyRequest.description: The answer to one pending input.

url.description: The URL the host used to show the notebook, with the host's token omitted.

changes.description: The changes, applied in order as one unit.

Change.description: One change to the document, tagged on `kind`.

base_etag.description: The document's `order_etag` as last read, or `*`.

order.description: Every cell id exactly once, in the new order, counting cells this edit creates and leaving out cells it deletes.

id.description: The cell to remove.

base_etag.description: The cell's etag as last read, or `*`.
The cell's etag as last read, or `*`.

ReplaceCell.description: Replaces an existing cell in place. A missing cell is a failed precondition.

id.description: The cell's id. A client chooses the id of a cell it creates.

name.description: The cell's name. `_` for an anonymous cell.

CellInput.description: A cell as a client writes it. Code must be a string, even when the host withholds source in cell records. Null is not an edit or a request to preserve existing source. The host derives the etags.

CellConfigInput.description: A cell's settings as a client writes them. A field left out takes its default.

CreateCell.description: Appends a new cell. An existing id is a failed precondition.

path.description: Where to put the file, relative to the project root and written the way the host's operating system writes paths.

name.description: A label to show people. In a project with a root it defaults to the filename.

CreateNotebookRequest.description: The notebook's own fields, minus what the host assigns. A project with a root requires `path`; one without requires `name`.

hostToken.description:
The `token` from a host record, sent as `Authorization: Bearer
<token>` on every request. Hosts accept the token only in that
header and omit CORS headers. Hosts answer only requests that arrive
over the machine's own loopback interface. Clients disable redirects
to keep authenticated requests on that interface.
